The Machine Intelligence Research Institute, or MIRI, is a nonprofit founded in 2000 and headquartered in Berkeley, California, United States. Its website describes it as an organization focused on preventing human extinction from artificial superintelligence. MIRI says it has worked for over two decades to understand and prepare for the challenges it expects humanity to face in a transition to a world with artificial superintelligence.

The institute states that its technical and philosophical work helped found the field of AI alignment, and that its researchers originated many of the theories and concepts central to current discussions of AI. It also argues that recent rapid advances at the frontier of artificial intelligence have sharply shortened estimates of when superintelligence will arrive, while progress on safety, alignment, and control has not kept up. In MIRI's account, humanity does not understand the internal workings of present systems well enough to fully control them or robustly steer their behavior, let alone more powerful systems expected later.

No lawsuits against the institute are recorded, and its legal exposure is listed under California with a count of 270. No products and no MCP servers are listed for it.
